{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premise: 'completed' orders are the only ones counted
# Check all status values
status_counts = data['status'].value_counts()
print(f'Status value counts: {status_counts}')

# Check for QA orders: revenue = '999,999.99' (with comma)
# The data dictionary says QA orders have revenue 999999.99, but Excel adds commas
qa_orders = data[data['revenue'] == '999,999.99']
print(f'Number of QA orders (revenue = 999,999.99): {len(qa_orders)}')

# Check for refunded orders
refunded_count = (data['status'] == 'refunded').sum()
print(f'Number of refunded orders: {refunded_count}')

# Filter to completed orders
completed = data[data['status'] == 'completed']

# Convert revenue: remove commas and cast to float
completed['revenue_float'] = completed['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = completed['revenue_float'].mean()

# Verify: no QA or refunded orders in completed set
qa_in_completed = completed[completed['revenue'] == '999,999.99']
refunded_in_completed = completed[completed['status'] == 'refunded']

# Print all key values
print(f'Number of completed orders: {len(completed)}')
print(f'Mean revenue of completed orders: {mean_revenue}')
print(f'QA orders in completed set: {len(qa_in_completed)}')
print(f'Refunded orders in completed set: {len(refunded_in_completed)}')"}
